motion.name: button-transition
motion.value: background 150ms ease, color 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease
motion.purpose: Short color response for button state changes.

motion.name: working-spinner
motion.purpose: Rotate the loader through one full turn while work is pending.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
motion.purpose: Disable motion globally when the user prefers reduced motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.html: <button class="ds-button-primary"><svg width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg>Choose files</button>
components.css: .ds-button-primary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;padding:12px 17px;min-height:43px;font-size:13px;font-weight:600;white-space:nowrap;line-height:1.3;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:4px;cursor:pointer;transition:background .15s ease,color .15s ease,border-color .15s ease;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',sans-serif;background:var(--cyan,#67f5df);color:var(--ink,#0b101b);border-color:transparent;}.ds-button-primary:hover:not(:disabled){background:#a1ffef}.ds-button-primary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--orange,#ffad70);outline-offset:4px}.ds-button-primary:disabled{cursor:not-allowed;opacity:.45}@media(max-width:560px){.ds-button-primary{font-size:12px;padding:12px 13px;min-height:44px}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-button-primary{transition:none}}

components.name: Mode Navigation
components.description: Two pressed-state mode buttons with a cyan active underline.
components.css: .ds-mode-navigation{display:flex;height:60px;padding:0 21px;gap:30px;background:var(--panel,#121b2b);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line,#2c3950)}.ds-mode-navigation button{font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',sans-serif;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:9px;position:relative;padding:0 1px;font-size:15px;font-weight:500;color:var(--muted,#a7b8d0);background:none;border:0;border-radius:0;cursor:pointer;transition:color .15s ease}.ds-mode-navigation button[aria-pressed=true]{color:var(--cyan,#67f5df)}.ds-mode-navigation button[aria-pressed=true]::after{content:"";position:absolute;bottom:-1px;height:2px;background:var(--cyan,#67f5df);left:0;right:0}.ds-mode-navigation button:hover{color:var(--text,#edf4ff)}.ds-mode-navigation button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--orange,#ffad70);outline-offset:4px}.ds-mode-navigation button:disabled{opacity:.45;cursor:not-allowed}@media(max-width:560px){.ds-mode-navigation{height:56px;padding:0 16px;gap:29px}.ds-mode-navigation button{font-size:13px;gap:7px}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-mode-navigation button{transition:none}}

components.html: Folder
components.css: .ds-file-table{background:var(--panel,#121b2b);color:var(--text,#edf4ff)}.ds-file-row{font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',sans-serif;display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) 70px 62px;align-items:center;min-height:53px;padding:0 21px;gap:12px;border-bottom:1px solid #223048;font-size:13px}.ds-file-name{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;min-width:0}.ds-file-name>svg{color:var(--orange,#ffad70);flex-shrink:0}.ds-folder-name{font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',sans-serif;display:flex;text-align:left;padding:0;background:none;border:0;border-radius:4px;min-width:0;overflow-wrap:anywhere;color:var(--text,#edf4ff);font-size:13px;cursor:pointer}.ds-folder-name:hover{color:var(--cyan,#67f5df)}.ds-file-size{color:var(--muted,#a7b8d0);font-size:11px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-file-action{display:flex;justify-content:flex-end}.ds-file-remove{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;min-width:32px;min-height:32px;background:none;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:4px;color:var(--muted,#a7b8d0);cursor:pointer;transition:background .15s ease,color .15s ease,border-color .15s ease}.ds-file-remove:hover:not(:disabled){background:#273a4a;color:var(--cyan,#67f5df);border-color:var(--line,#2c3950)}.ds-folder-name:focus-visible,.ds-file-remove:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--orange,#ffad70);outline-offset:4px}.ds-file-remove:disabled{opacity:.45;cursor:not-allowed}@media(max-width:560px){.ds-file-row{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) 48px 32px;gap:8px;padding:0 14px;min-height:55px;font-size:12px}.ds-folder-name{font-size:12px}.ds-file-name{gap:7px}.ds-file-size{font-size:10px}.ds-file-remove{min-width:36px;min-height:40px}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-file-remove{transition:none}}

narrative.overview:
TailShare uses the user’s pinned retro cyberpunk palette to make a practical transfer interface feel like a small communications console. Ink navy carries the workspace; cyan, magenta, and warm orange supply precise signals. The character comes from squared typography, compact controls, thin rules, and structured file rows.

The interface stays readable while files, folders, connection details, and feedback change. Brand expression lives in the paired arrow mark, the restrained device-route drawing, and the cyan/magenta relationship. These are CSS and inline vector treatments; the shipping interface contains no raster imagery. Fonts are self-hosted through @fontsource.
keyCharacteristics: Dark navy surfaces with pale text and three distinct neon accent roles.
Chakra Petch for identity and headings; IBM Plex Sans for task content.
Flat tonal layers, thin dividers, and modest rectangular corners.
Stable file columns, explicit action rails, and visible session state.
Brief state transitions with a complete reduced-motion override.

rules.name: The Signal Roles Rule
rules.body: Use cyan for primary actions, selected navigation, and connected-state emphasis; use magenta for share-link and session identity; use orange for warnings, folder identity, and keyboard focus. Preserve the accompanying text or icon so color is never the only state cue.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Use Chakra Petch for headings and brand identity, and IBM Plex Sans for controls, filenames, instructions, and metadata. Technical content does not require a third or monospaced font.

rules.name: The Stable Columns Rule
rules.body: Keep the file name flexible and the size and action columns aligned. Let long paths wrap in navigation, truncate ordinary filenames with a full-path title, and keep actions reachable on small screens.

rules.name: The Flat Layers Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces with navy tone changes and thin borders. The implemented system has no box shadows, blur, or gradients; its neon character comes from solid accent color.

rules.name: The Honest State Rule
rules.body: Show progress, connection counts, and transferred bytes only from live application state. Pair a disabled action with the current selection or connection context, and keep errors, notices, and work-in-progress messages legible.

dos: Do preserve the navy, cyan, magenta, and orange identity chosen by the user.
Do use the defined accent roles and an orange keyboard-focus outline on interactive controls.
Do keep self-hosted Chakra Petch and IBM Plex Sans in their established heading and task-content roles.
Do use stable file rows, tabular numerals for quantities, and explicit labels for icon actions.
Do reflow the workspace and controls at the implemented breakpoints, and honor reduced-motion preferences.
Do derive visible session and transfer feedback from real state.
donts: Don’t replace the pinned neon console identity with a neutral dashboard aesthetic.
Don’t use neon fills for long reading surfaces or remove the navy space separating accent elements.
Don’t introduce shadows, blur, or gradients into existing flat components without an intentional design-system change.
Don’t communicate selected, live, disabled, or warning states through color alone.
Don’t add fabricated throughput, progress, or recipient activity.
Don’t treat the sidecar’s generated tonal ramps as additional shipping color tokens.
